text:
sofia: heads-up — us-west gpu fleet experienced a sudden saturation event ~10m ago. small-models queue spiked and hotpath tail latency climbed.

ops-bot: [alert] 1903456792 - cluster-us-west-2b gpu-util=98% queue_depth=620 p99_latency=2.3s :warning:

ben: seeing it too. pattern = lots of sub-50-token requests; heavy KV cache churn + short TTLs. warm-pool for small-models sat at min=3, not enough for this microburst.

sofia: is this one customer or multi-tenant? any big fanout we can attribute?

aneesh: multi-tenant. looks like an organic PLG spike + a partner campaign causing fanout. qps delta hit ~5x baseline over 90s.

maria: oncall summary: queue TTLs were exceeded for some requests and the admission controller performed soft-shedding (no 5xx returned, but several p90/p99 SLOs breached for ~12m).

ben: immediate mitigations we applied:
- bumped warm_pool.min from 3 -> 10 for pool-small-models
- increased token_bucket.refill_rate to 220 and capacity to 1200
- enabled short-term per-route qps caps for the heaviest chat routes

kai: we should avoid manual bumps long-term. proposal: delta-driven prewarm (trigger when qps_delta > 25% sustained for 20s) + a small burst credit allowance for PLG/free tiers.

aneesh: also saw NIC egress nearing 82% in the AZ. prewarm must consider NIC and network egress limits; otherwise you just add nodes that saturate egress and don't help latency.

ben: pushing a quick canary with the warm_pool change now.

ops-bot: deploy started by ben at 1903456805 — rolling update pool-small-models (2/2 hosts updated).

maria: observability checklist for the canary:
- queue_depth, admitted/rejected counts per-route
- p90/p99 latency for hotpath routes
- sample traces of queued requests to verify KV cache miss ratio
- cost delta monitor: alert if running GPUs increase >20% for >10m

ben: quick metric query:
```
# last 30m queue depth for small-models
curl -s "https://obs.internal/api/metrics?metric=queue_depth&pool=small-models&window=30m" | jq .
```

sofia: after the canary we saw queue_depth drop 620 -> 95 in ~90s, p90 restored to baseline, p99 improving. no client 5xx spikes.

kai: cost impact? we need a policy to weigh SLO preservation vs extra prewarmed nodes.

maria: warm_pool bump added ~8 nodes during the peak — estimated incremental cost ~+$1.10 for the event. Finance says acceptable as a one-off to avoid SLO breaches for PLG.

aneesh: follow-ups to track:
- implement delta-driven prewarm heuristic (qps_delta threshold + sustain window)
- admission controller: two-tier token buckets (hotpath fast tokens, coldpath conservative tokens)
- soft backpressure signal to clients: 429 + Retry-After when queue TTL exceeded and TTL-shed applied
- NIC-aware prewarm: skip prewarming if az_egress_util > 80% or if per-tenant egress cap would be exceeded

ben: also adding cooldown to prewarm trigger to avoid oscillation: require sustained qps_delta > 25% for 30s before expanding warm_pool.

sofia: please add warm_pool_utilization metric to the console so product can see efficiency and tradeoffs.

ops-bot: scaling events logged: scale_up +8 nodes @1903456810, scale_down scheduled in 20m if utilization < 35%.

maria: filing tickets for infra + admission + obs. i'll coordinate a short post-incident note and tag billing for automated emergency-policy discussion.

ben: PRs to be opened:
- infra: delta-prewarm-heuristic (#4892)
- admission: hot-cold-token-bucket (#4893)
- obs: warm_pool_utilization metric + cost-alert (#4894)

sofia: sounds good — monitor for the next 24h and if pattern repeats we'll roll the heuristic globally. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: closing oncall thread; will escalate to program if recurrence happens.
